<!-- pr-reviewer: 08f1f9ff5a6eb13fbe4465feeedad8c598f5a446 -->
Review: blockers (2). Read-only review. No build: the PR changes docs and process files only.

**Blockers**

1. `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md:150-152` (unchanged text) disagrees with the new law. It says: "A conflicting PR of ours that waits for the merge batch therefore stays a draft until merge time. The merging session refreshes it". Under **Own blocked PRs first**, our own conflicting PR is refreshed before the next new issue, not at merge time. Edit this paragraph so that it names the new law as the exception for our own PRs.
2. `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md:275-277` (unchanged text) and `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md:72-77` (unchanged text) also keep the old rule without the exception:
   - merge-ready: "Open PRs this batch turned `CONFLICTING` ... are left alone ... They are refreshed when their turn to merge comes."
   - resolve-conflicts: "Work only on the PR the merge batch is about to merge ... Never every `CONFLICTING` PR at once: an early refresh is undone by the next merge to main".
   Add one sentence to each: our own PRs are refreshed under **Own blocked PRs first** (one PR for each worker). Check (2) of the brief is "no contradiction left anywhere", so these must agree too.

**Checked and correct**

- The new law in `AGENTS.md:196-208` agrees with the maintainer's words in #3133: own PRs, labels `conflicts` and `needs-rework`, fix before a new issue. The label name `needs-rework` is correct.
- The #681 format has the reload part in `AGENTS.md:183-186`, in `merge-ready` and in `review-prs`.
- The check is in `work-issue` step 0, in `coordinator.md` and in the four `issue-worker-*.md` files.
- The PR body has `Process change: yes`. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is not changed. The bold rule names did not change, and the new name is cited correctly. Each changed file has 0 CR bytes.

**Text that goes beyond the maintainer's words (not blockers)**

- "A PR whose issue has `claimed` is already in work and is skipped." This supports the law: it prevents two fixes of one PR.
- `work-issue` step 0: a worker does not fix a listed PR. It stops, reports the PR numbers, and the coordinator sends a worker. This supports the law, because the system still fixes the PR before the new issue. But `AGENTS.md:200` says "It fixes each one". Recommended: "It fixes each one, or sends a worker to fix it." Then the law and step 0 agree.
- `work-issue` step 0 also skips "the PR that your brief names". This is necessary and correct.

**Notes (not blockers)**

- The four `issue-worker-*.md` files point to step 0 and do not repeat the commands. `coordinator.md:26-27` shortens the second command to `--label needs-rework`. Recommended: write the full second command, the same as in `work-issue`.
- `AGENTS.md:373-375`: "It takes `git merge origin/main` only then, when it is the next PR in a merge batch, or when ..." is not clear. Recommended: a vertical list of the three cases.
- A possible race: if the coordinator sends a fix worker and a new-issue worker at the same time, the new-issue worker can stop before the fix worker sets `claimed`. The coordinator text says "before the new issue", so the order prevents this.

Review fixes on head 68c6f67f2f4a607b71b91d4218eaf8d3f34ab1cc (plain push, the PR stays a draft):

- `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md`: a conflicting PR of ours stays a draft until its author's agents fix it under "Own blocked PRs first", or until merge time.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md` "Don't refresh the rest": the author's agents can refresh earlier under "Own blocked PRs first".
- `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md` contributor mode: the author's own `conflicts` PRs under "Own blocked PRs first" are a permitted target.
- `AGENTS.md` **Own blocked PRs first**: "fixes each one, or sends a worker to fix it".
- `AGENTS.md` **Refresh only at merge time**: the three cases are now a list.
- `.claude/agents/coordinator.md`: the second `gh pr list` command is written in full.

Docs and process files only. No build. Each changed file has 0 CR bytes.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 68c6f67f2f4a607b71b91d4218eaf8d3f34ab1cc -->
Review: clean. Read-only review of commit 68c6f67f2 (the change after 08f1f9ff5). No build: the PR changes docs and process files only.

- Blocker 1 is fixed. `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md:150-152` now names **Own blocked PRs first** as the exception for our own PRs.
- Blocker 2 is fixed. `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md:277-278` and `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md:74-77` now name the exception.
- The suggestions are applied:
  - `AGENTS.md:200` says "or sends a worker to fix it".
  - `AGENTS.md:371-379` lists the three cases.
  - `coordinator.md:27` has the full second command.
- Check (2) on the whole tree: no line in a process file states the old refresh rule without the own-PR exception. The remaining "Refresh only at merge time" citations are in `fork-sync`, `release-cut` step 2, `merge-ready` step 3 and the maintainer mode of `resolve-conflicts`. Each one is about the merging session, a cut or a contributor PR. They do not disagree with the new law.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is not changed. Each changed file has 0 CR bytes.

Note (not a blocker): `AGENTS.md:200`, `.claude/agents/coordinator.md:27` and `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md:152` are longer than the 80-column wrap of the files near them.

Ready and merge: the coordinator flags head 68c6f67f2 ready and merges it. It is a docs and process PR (Process change: yes). Review: the Opus review (comment 7061095820 on 08f1f9ff5, two blockers) and the re-review on this head (comment 7061120424, clean). PROCESS_VERSION is not edited; the bump PR follows.
